keyVerseText: And it was so, that when they that bare the ark of the LORD had gone six paces, he sacrificed oxen and fatlings.
rootMeaning: The root of מְרִיא (mᵉrîyʼ) is מָרָא (mârâʼ), which carries connotations of grossness and rebellion, even suggesting a domineering or overpowering nature. This etymology enriches the understanding of מְרִיא beyond the simple notion of a 'fat beast' by implying an animal that is not only well-fed but also possesses a commanding presence or strength. The progression from a root meaning related to filth and rebellion to a noun describing a fatling suggests a transformation from unruliness to a state of abundance and provision.
usageInScripture: The word מְרִיא appears eight times in Scripture, consistently referring to well-fed or fat beasts, often in the context of sacrificial animals. It is translated variously as 'fat cattle,' 'fatlings,' or 'fed beasts,' highlighting its association with animals prepared for offering or celebration. This consistent usage underscores the term's link to abundance, provision, and the honoring of God through sacrifice, emphasizing the value of offering the best and most nourishing animals.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding מְרִיא as denoting a fat, well-fed beast used in sacrifice deepens our appreciation for the biblical emphasis on offering God the best of what we have. The root's implication of strength and dominance transformed into a symbol of provision reminds believers that God is sovereign over all creation and worthy of our finest gifts. This word points to the richness of God's blessings and the call to respond with gratitude and reverence. It also subtly reflects the transformation from rebellion to restoration found in the gospel, where what was once dominated by sin is made whole and pleasing in God's sight.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Samuel 6:13, the phrase 'he sacrificed oxen and fatlings' uses מְרִיא to emphasize the quality of the offerings accompanying the ark of the LORD. The presence of fatlings signals a celebration marked by abundance and reverence, highlighting the significance of honoring God with well-prepared, valuable sacrifices. This word enriches the verse by portraying the offerings as not merely routine but as expressions of joy and devotion, reflecting the blessed presence of God among His people.
